entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Tielman Susato, active primarily in Antwerp from the 1540s until his death around 1570, stands as a pivotal figure in the history of Renaissance music, not only as a prolific composer and instrumentalist but more significantly as the first prominent music publisher in the Low Countries. His enterprise at the sign of 'Den Cromhorn' (The Crumhorn) played a crucial role in disseminating the works of the Franco-Flemish school, including masterpieces by Orlande de Lassus and Josquin des Prez, alongside his own compositions. Susato's dual role as a creative artist and a shrewd businessman highlights the emerging commercialization of music in 16th-century Europe, establishing Antwerp as a vibrant hub for musical innovation and distribution.

Between 1543 and 1561, Susato published an astonishing volume of music, including over fifty collections of chansons, masses, motets, and instrumental pieces. His most celebrated undertaking, the *Musyck Boexken* (Music Books), comprised a series of volumes showcasing both sacred and secular polyphony, including his influential collection of instrumental dance music, *Het derde musyck boexken: Danserye* (1551). This publication provided an invaluable snapshot of the period's popular dances—such as allemandes, pavanes, and galliards—and facilitated their widespread performance by amateur and professional musicians alike. Susato was also among the first to publish music specifically for instrumental ensembles, a testament to his foresight in catering to a growing market beyond vocal polyphony.
